Subject: Vector store migration playbook & onboarding for CanyonAnalytics

Hi Evan/Marta,

Following up from last week's partner sync — CanyonAnalytics (cc'd) is planning to migrate their vector stack from our current pgvector PoC to a managed pilot (Pinecone and Weaviate both under consideration) with an S3 cold-store tier for long-term snapshots. They asked us to provide a single, clear migration playbook they can share internally and to confirm typical timelines, uplift work, and a pilot scope for evaluation.

High-level asks from CanyonAnalytics:
- Pilot environment for ~12M vectors (initial import) with 1536-d embeddings
- Steady-state query load ~200 qps, spikes to ~1k qps for short windows
- Cold-storage to S3 (monthly snapshots + incremental) and ability to reconstruct indexes from snapshots
- Clear MAP (mutual action plan), cost estimate, and security evidence (SOC2 / data handling guidance)

I've attached a rough migration checklist and an architecture sketch to start (migration-checklist.xlsx, arch-diagram.png). Can you each confirm:
1) Typical time-to-onboard for a 12M vector dataset and who on your side would be the point for ingestion support.
2) Any constraints / gotchas about metadata, namespaces, or ID schemas we should call out.
3) S3 snapshot/replay patterns you recommend (format, frequency, restore time expectations).

Preferred kickoff windows: week of July 6 or July 13. Let me know availability.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Evan Li <evan@pinecone.io>

Subject: Re: Vector store migration playbook & onboarding for CanyonAnalytics

Sergio — thanks for the context and the checklist. Quick responses below; happy to jump on a call next week.

1) Time-to-onboard: for a 12M vector dataset we typically see a 2-3 week pilot to full index depending on ingestion parallelism and whether vectors need re-normalization. For an initial trial where you push a full snapshot, plan on ~48-72 hours for bulk import if you can provide files in our recommended format.
2) Point of contact: Evan Li (me) for pilot coordination; Engineering contact: Priya on our onboard team (priya@pinecone.io).
3) Metadata / namespaces: Pinecone treats namespace as the fastest partitioning; avoid using very high cardinality namespaces per query. If you expect heavy multi-tenant joins, suggest a single namespace with metadata tags instead. IDs should be stable (avoid opaque auto-generated IDs during migration).
4) Snapshots: we support export to S3 in ndjson + vector payload or flat binary (recommended for speed). For your size, a monthly full snapshot + daily deltas is reasonable. Restore time is largely IO-bound; estimate 6-10 hours for full rebuild on a dedicated import node.

Security evidence: we can share a SOC2 summary and our security whitepaper — I'll attach the standard package to the hub link after this note.

Available July 7-9 for a kickoff; if that works I can block time with our solutions engineer.

—Evan
Evan Li
Partnerships Manager, Pinecone
evan@pinecone.io

From: Marta López <marta@weaviate-partners.com>

Subject: Re: Vector store migration playbook & onboarding for CanyonAnalytics

Sergio / Evan — quick technical notes from the Weaviate side that we recommend including in the playbook:

- Namespaces vs. Shards: Weaviate uses classes and shard keys; map your tenant/namespace design to class metadata to avoid cross-class queries.
- Embedding / dimension alignment: confirm the embedding model and ensure vectors are L2-normalized if your similarity metric requires it.
- Snapshot format: Weaviate supports S3 bucket snapshots via our backup tool (tar.gz of objects + manifest). For 12M vectors expect a ~8-12 hour backup window depending on parallelism.
- Rehydration: rehydrating into a managed cluster is straightforward but you should version your manifest so any transform scripts are repeatable.

Edge caveat: if you plan on migrating live traffic (blue/green), ensure duplicate IDs are deduped at ingest and plan for a short catch-up window where both systems accept writes.

Happy to provide a sample backup script and a short runbook.

—Marta
Marta López
Integration Engineer, Weaviate Partners
marta@weaviate-partners.com

Thanks Sergio, Evan, Marta — helpful detail. A few specifics from our side so estimates are grounded:

- Vector count: ~12,000,000 (12M) initial; steady growth ~500k vectors/month.
- Embedding: 1536 dims (OpenEmbed v2), 16 bytes per float (we're using float32).
- Ingest pattern: nightly batch loads + occasional realtime writes (up to 1k qps bursts).
- Security: must see SOC2 Type II excerpt and data handling controls. Procurement will require a vendor form (attached).
- Legal: we prefer limited liability in the MOU and a 60-day pilot with an option to convert to a committed contract.

Could both vendors provide ballpark cost ranges for the pilot and a rough timeline so our CFO can greenlight the POC spend? We'd like to pick between a Pinecone-managed and a Weaviate-managed option by July 16.

Julia Park
Head of Platform, CanyonAnalytics
